land.text: Kammanu, 'a Luwian (Neo-Hittite) state centred on Melid', the infobox successor

successors.note: The page says a new state emerged after the Hittite collapse in the early 12th century BC; Kammanu paid tribute to Tiglath-Pileser I (1115-1077 BC) and its city was sacked by Sargon II in 712 BC. Cliopatria's Neo-Hittite shapes of -1150 and later may or may not cover the Elazig plain.

correction.text: Isuwa on the eastern bank of the Euphrates facing Malatya: Tunceli Province and the Altinova plain round Elazig, with the Murat valleys

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Isuwa (its Hittite shape of -1300 covers the area from the empire period). The page gives no area; it places Isuwa 'on the eastern bank of the river Euphrates' facing Malatya, in modern Tunceli Province, with the Altinova plain and the Murat valleys; much of the land lies under the Keban, Karakaya, Ataturk and Birecik reservoirs. Tunceli plus Elazig (about 17,000 km2) is the researcher's reading.

The page gives no founding date; it says Isuwa was 'under Hittite sovereignty from c. 1600 BC', so this is a bridging judgment at the first hostile act.

notes: Cliopatria has no Isuwa; the Hittite shape of -1300 (320,000 km2) covers the Elazig plain. The Isuwa page has no founding, capital, area or Mitanni-overlordship dates, so every event is a bridge at confidence 1-2 and the state is drawn only from the first dated hostility (c. 1400) to the empire's fall. Isuwa was 'under Hittite sovereignty from c. 1600 BC', so 1400-1350 as an independent or Mitanni-allied land is the page's story of hostility, not a surveyed border. The hittites dossier (me-04-a) notes Isuwa overrun in the One-Year War and does not draw it; the renderer should draw Isuwa as the Hittite vassal tint from 1350. Kammanu (Melid) belongs to the Neo-Hittite states dossier; the Isuwa page dates it only by Tiglath-Pileser I and Sargon II. The page also has Hattusili I (c. 1600 BC) 'marched his army across the Euphrates river' into the land before the dossier's span (not listed as a war). Page budget: two pages.
